label: monopoly99-probe
_why: Does WORLD_MARKET_MONOPOLY_MIN_SHARE 0.99 (vanilla 0.5) change anything? (user, 2026-10-17: 'run several probes directly on latest autosaves to determine whether setting WORLD_MARKET_MONOPOLY_MIN_SHARE to 0.99 would affect anything'). Vanilla raises a good's WORLD MARKET price by up to MONOPOLY_PRICE_IMPACT 0.2 when one market controls more than the min share of its exports. In the user's Japan playtest (canon build of 2026-10-16 20:42) Japan's market holds 50-99% of world exports of steel 98.2%, groceries 99.0%, luxury furniture, lead, clothes 87.5%, telephones, furniture, merchant marine, luxury clothes, silk, porcelain, small arms, fine art, tools 51.1%, dye 50.4% (1935.1.1) - those lose the markup at 0.99; explosives, paper, glass, cars 99.9%, steamers, fertilizer, radios, ammunition, sulfur and aeroplanes sit at 99.9-100% and KEEP it. Each run CONTINUES one of the user's own autosaves (copies in Documents/.../save games BACKUP 20261017_1858) for one in-game year, PAIRED by start save: the canon and the probe from the same save, plus a canon repeat from the 1935 save to measure run-to-run noise.

_arms.canon: {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.json} - the canon jex-dam4s-rs-x25-m10ac-dpriv (sha256 fc7490eb6288514b), proven byte-identical to the user's deployed 2026-10-16 20:42 build apart from the build stamps; + telemetry
_arms.mono99: {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.monopoly99-probe.json} - the canon + game_defines.NEconomy.WORLD_MARKET_MONOPOLY_MIN_SHARE 0.99, nothing else (field diff: game_defines + the _monopoly_probe record; build diff: the NEconomy block and the config name in header comments); + telemetry

_comparison: Per start save, mono99 against canon at the end of the year: the world market price of every good from the save's 52-week ring (weekly path), Japan's market's exports and every country's imports (save summaries), and the tagged markets' local prices and trade (market_goods_scoped, quarterly). The canon repeat from the 1935 save says how far two runs from one save drift apart without any change.

_predictions.affected goods: world price lower in mono99 by up to ~0.2 x share (steel, clothes, luxury clothes, furniture, lead, silk, porcelain, telephones, tools, dye, groceries): visible within weeks of the start
_predictions.unaffected goods: explosives, paper, glass, cars, steamers, fertilizer at 100% share: no change beyond run-to-run noise
_predictions.second order: importers' local prices of the affected goods fall less than the world price (capacity-capped, F161); Japan's export volume rises a little; a year is too short for production to respond

_stop_rule: none: a fixed n=5, every run plays its year.
_cost: 5 runs x 1 in-game year (1934->1935 or 1935->1936) from a late save, about 6-9 min each with monthly autosaves, about 35-45 min
_caveats: The saves are a PLAYER game (Japan). Under -handsoff the loaded country may stay player-controlled with no input: identical in both arms, so the A/B holds, but Japan makes no decisions for a year.
The observer's autosaves overwrite the user's autosave slots and continue_game.json: the backup holds the originals, restored after the batch.
Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 CALLED DIRECTLY from the PowerShell tool (landmine L30). Not a 2+1 batch: no stop watcher.
